World Series Game 1 is TONIGHT.

Nick Martinez starts for Tampa Bay.
Jacob Misiorowski starts for Milwaukee.

American Family Field | 8:07 PM ET | FOX
Brewers -162 | Rays +134

Neither team has ever won a World Series.
Tonight that changes.

#WorldSeries #Brewers #Rays

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Game 1 checklist:

✅ American Family Field SOLD OUT
✅ Misiorowski confirmed (MIL)
✅ Martinez confirmed (TB)
✅ Brewers 4-0 home this postseason
✅ First World Series title ever on the line

8:07 PM ET | FOX

#WorldSeries #Brewers #Rays

facebook.long_form:
Tonight is the night.

The 2026 World Series begins at American Family Field in Milwaukee when the Tampa Bay Rays visit the Brewers for Game 1. First pitch is 8:07 PM Eastern on FOX. Admission sold out months ago, but the broadcast will be available to everyone.

Here is what we know: Jacob Misiorowski takes the mound for Milwaukee. The presumptive NL Cy Young winner led the league in ERA and strikeouts during the regular season at 16-5, 1.80 ERA. His postseason has featured shorter outings than his regular-season work, but he is well-rested and throwing for a franchise that has been waiting 44 years for this moment.

On the other side, ESPN confirmed the Rays will send Nick Martinez in Game 1 — not Drew Rasmussen, which surprises many analysts who expected their ace to go first. The tactical decision means Rasmussen is available in full for Game 2 tomorrow night, still at American Family Field.

Milwaukee is favored (-162) with Tampa Bay at +134. The Brewers went 4-0 at home this postseason. Neither team has won a World Series in franchise history. One of these groups changes that tonight.

stories.title: Freddy Peralta Is Coming Back to Milwaukee — As the Enemy

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Freddy Peralta spent 8 seasons as a Milwaukee Brewer.

They traded him in January.

He went 2-0, 0.75 ERA in the ALCS. Won ALCS MVP.

Now he's coming BACK to Milwaukee to pitch against them in the World Series.

This storyline writes itself. #WorldSeries #Rays

facebook.long_form:
There is no subplot more fitting for the 2026 World Series than the story of Freddy Peralta.

Peralta spent eight seasons as a Milwaukee Brewer. He became one of the program's signature arms — a Dominican-born right-hander whose fastball and breaking ball combination made him a fan favorite at American Family Field. Last year he went 17-6 with a 2.70 ERA in his final Brewers season.

Then the Brewers traded him. In January 2026, with Peralta eligible for free agency, Milwaukee sent him to the New York Mets. It was a business decision — the kind teams make regularly. The Mets then traded him to Tampa Bay at the deadline.

Peralta rewarded the Rays immediately. In the ALCS against the Cleveland Guardians, he went 2-0 with a 0.75 ERA across three appearances including two starts. He pitched 5.1 innings in the clinching Game 6 and was named ALCS Most Valuable Player.

Now he's heading back to Milwaukee. As the opponent.

Whether he starts Game 2 or Game 3, Peralta will stand on the mound in front of the fans who cheered for him for eight years — and try to deny them the championship they have been waiting for their entire lives.
facebook.image_caption: Freddy Peralta spent 8 years as a Brewer. Now he's coming back as Tampa Bay's ALCS MVP. The World Series just got even more compelling.

article.headline: Freddy Peralta Is Coming Back to Milwaukee — This Time as the Enemy

stories.title: Drew Rasmussen Has Been Untouchable — And He Hasn't Pitched Yet

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Drew Rasmussen in the 2026 playoffs:

16-5, 2.67 ERA in regular season
1.29 ERA in 21 playoff innings
Near no-hitter vs Yankees in ALDS Game 1

He doesn't pitch TONIGHT.

He goes Game 2. Against the best home team in baseball.

#Rays #WorldSeries

facebook.long_form:
The Rays are not starting their best pitcher tonight. That is, in a strange way, a statement of confidence.

Drew Rasmussen had one of the most dominant postseason runs a starting pitcher has produced in years. In 21 innings across the ALDS and ALCS, he posted a 1.29 ERA. In Game 1 of the ALDS against the Yankees, he carried a no-hitter into the late innings before settling for a one-hitter and a 1-0 victory with 10 strikeouts. He then threw seven innings in ALCS Game 5, allowing just one run, to push the Rays to the brink of the pennant.

In the regular season he went 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA and made the All-Star Game for the second consecutive year.

Tampa Bay's decision to open with Nick Martinez tonight — rather than Rasmussen — means their postseason ace will step in for Game 2, fully rested, still at American Family Field. The Brewers will face their most dangerous challenge in Game 2, not Game 1.

For a franchise built on analytical deployment, using Rasmussen out of turn in Game 1 would have been a short-term decision. The Rays are playing for the series, not just the opener.
facebook.image_caption: Drew Rasmussen: 1.29 ERA in 21 playoff innings. Near no-hitter vs. the Yankees. He doesn't pitch tonight. He goes Game 2 in Milwaukee. The Rays' best option is still coming.

article.headline: Drew Rasmussen Has Been Untouchable This Postseason — And He Hasn't Pitched Yet

stories.title: First-Time Champion Guaranteed — The Historical Stakes of Brewers vs. Rays

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Tonight's World Series guarantees history.

Brewers: 0 titles (last appearance: 1982)
Rays: 0 titles (appeared in 2008 and 2020)

One of these droughts ends this October.

44 years of waiting. 18 years of trying.

Something is going to change. #WorldSeries

facebook.long_form:
When the final out is recorded in this World Series, a city is going to celebrate its first championship in franchise history. That is guaranteed.

The Milwaukee Brewers last appeared in the World Series in 1982. They pushed the St. Louis Cardinals to seven games at old County Stadium before falling. Since then, a generation of Brewers fans has grown up without ever seeing their team win it all. The franchise joined the National League in 1998 and has rebuilt multiple times, finally arriving at this moment with their best team in decades — 103 regular-season wins, the most in baseball.

The Tampa Bay Rays have appeared in two previous World Series. In 2008, they shocked the baseball world by reaching the Fall Classic in only their 11th franchise season before losing to the Philadelphia Phillies in five games. In 2020, they made it back, building a two-games-to-one series lead before the Los Angeles Dodgers won four straight. The Rays have been close twice without closing.

Tonight opens the third chance for Tampa Bay and the second for Milwaukee. The historical weight is equal on both sides. What is different now: neither team looks like a longshot. Both are legitimate contenders. Both have the arms, the depth, and the experience.

One of them is going to celebrate in the streets of their city this October.
facebook.image_caption: Brewers: 0 World Series titles. Last appearance: 1982. Rays: 0 World Series titles. Appeared in 2008 and 2020. Tonight, one of these droughts starts its final chapter.

article.headline: A First-Time Champion Is Guaranteed — The Historical Weight of Brewers vs. Rays

stories.title: Franco Caminero — The Rays' X-Factor in This World Series

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Franco Caminero in the 2026 playoffs:

• 45 HR, 110 RBI in 2025 (2x All-Star)
• .265/.356/.490, 13 HR in 51 games this fall
• Hit the foul-pole 2-run HR in ALCS Game 6

He's the Rays' X-factor in the World Series.

Caminero may decide this. #Rays #WorldSeries

facebook.long_form:
If you want to find the player most likely to swing this World Series in Tampa Bay's direction, look at the third baseman.

Franco Caminero's 2025 season was a revelation. He made his first two All-Star Games, finished with 45 home runs and 110 RBI, and established himself as one of the best young hitters in the American League at just 21 years old. This year, nagging injuries limited him to 51 games — but in those games, he was still dangerous: a .265/.356/.490 slash line with 13 home runs and 27 RBI.

Then came October.

In ALCS Game 6 — with the Rays one win from the World Series — Caminero hit a two-run home run off the foul pole in the seventh inning that proved to be the decisive blow in Tampa Bay's 7-3 victory. It was the kind of moment that announces a player to a national audience.

Milwaukee's pitching staff is elite. The Brewers bullpen posted a 0.38 ERA across 23.2 innings in the NLCS against the Dodgers. Misiorowski is the best starter in the National League. Getting to this staff is not easy.

But Caminero has done hard things before. The World Series is where legacies are made. Tonight, he gets his shot.
facebook.image_caption: Franco Caminero hit the foul-pole HR that sent the Rays to the World Series. Now he faces the best pitching staff in baseball. The X-factor enters the Fall Classic.

article.headline: Franco Caminero Is the Rays' X-Factor in the World Series — And He Already Has His Signature Moment
